subject: Mathematics
objective: Show why the tangent at a point on a unit circle is perpendicular to the radius.
learner: Knows circle geometry and basic sine/cosine.
requiredInteraction: Change angle and inspect the right angle.
correctnessCriteria: No claim that tangent touches elsewhere

subject: Physics
objective: Show how a ray bends when entering a denser medium and why the normal is a reference.
misconceptions: Light always bends toward the normal
The angle is measured from the surface
requiredInteraction: Change incidence angle or refractive index.
correctnessCriteria: No claim of total internal reflection unless applicable

subject: Chemistry
objective: Connect pressure, volume and temperature changes for a fixed amount of gas.
misconceptions: Pressure is the same as temperature
requiredInteraction: Change V or T and observe P.
correctnessCriteria: P and V inverse at fixed T

subject: Statistics
objective: Show how a positive test depends on base rate and sensitivity, not just test accuracy.
misconceptions: A 99% test means 99% probability of disease
correctnessCriteria: High sensitivity alone does not imply high posterior

subject: Mathematics
objective: Show a vector that keeps its direction under a linear transformation while its length scales.
correctnessCriteria: No claim every real matrix has real eigenvectors

subject: AI/ML
objective: Show a decision boundary and how predicted probability changes with a feature.
misconceptions: Logistic regression predicts a class directly with a straight line

subject: Computer Science
objective: Show divide, sort halves and merge in order.

subject: Computer Science
objective: Show inorder traversal visiting left subtree, node, right subtree.
misconceptions: Node is visited before left subtree
correctnessCriteria: No claim of sorted unless BST

subject: Computer Science
objective: Show why atomicity and rollback keep a transaction's partial writes invisible.
misconceptions: A failed transaction leaves partial writes

subject: Economics
objective: Show why individually rational choices can produce a worse collective outcome.
misconceptions: Nash equilibrium is always socially optimal
Cooperation is irrational in one shot
correctnessCriteria: Defect dominates in the specified game

subject: Economics
objective: Connect marginal cost to the cost of one more unit and to supply decisions.

subject: Statistics
objective: Show spread around the mean and why deviations are squared before averaging.
misconceptions: SD is the average absolute deviation
requiredInteraction: Add/remove an outlier or change spread.

subject: Computer Science
objective: Show why cache hits are faster than main-memory access and how locality helps.
misconceptions: Cache is always faster for every access
requiredInteraction: Change access pattern or cache size.

subject: Literature
objective: Help a learner recognize how a sonnet's turn and rhyme scheme shape meaning.
learner: Can read poetry but not scan form.
requiredInteraction: Mark the turn or compare two sonnets.
accessibility: text-first; audio alternative; no animation required

subject: Language Learning
objective: Help a learner distinguish denotation from connotation using near-synonyms in context.
misconceptions: Synonyms are interchangeable in every context
requiredInteraction: Choose the best word and justify it.
correctnessCriteria: No claim of one correct feeling
